youtube_title: Porter, Indiana: the 1921 railroad crossing wreck that killed 37
youtube:
37 people died at one railroad crossing in Porter, Indiana. On Sunday evening, February 27, 1921, the tower had set the signals for the New York Central's Interstate Express, and a Michigan Central train was told to stop. It didn't. It ran through a safety derail and onto the ties, and a wooden coach was on the crossing when the express arrived at about 50 miles an hour. Federal investigators said the engineer missed a stop signal; he said he thought he saw green, then lost it in smoke and steam. They also said the derail, 311 feet from the crossing, did not give the protection it was meant to.
